title: The Septuagint reads 'angels of God' in Genesis 6

tellings.quote: And in the Septuagent, when you read Genesis 6, it doesn't say the sons of God. It says the angels of God.

plain: Tim Alberino, a filmmaker and researcher, points to the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible. He says that in Genesis 6, a passage in the Bible's first book, the Septuagint does not say "the sons of God" but "the angels of God." He raises it because it would mean the beings in that passage were understood as angels rather than men.
